stories.headline: COP31 enters second day of overtime as fossil-fuel dispute blocks a climate deal

sources.body:
COP31 President ​Murat Kurum asks negotiators to consider a last-minute proposal in attempt to reach an agreement.

Turkish officials have asked negotiators at the COP31 climate summit to consider a last-minute proposal as talks stretched into a second day of overtime over the fossil fuels issue.

“We believe that we have put forward a text which all the parties can agree upon,” COP31 President Murat Kurum told a late-night plenary session on Saturday.

Kurum, who is also Turkiye’s environment minister, said the conference would reconvene later on Sunday morning to approve the deal.

The latest text was not immediately made public, and it was unclear if negotiators had received the wording overnight, which would give nations only a few hours to submit objections and changes.

An earlier draft had drawn strong condemnation for failing to mention fossil fuels, the largest contributors to climate change.

Kurum said he ⁠believed concerns around fossil fuels had ‌been addressed, as had those ‌around helping developing countries finance their adaptations to climate change.

The new ‌text followed intensive consultations between Australia, which is ‌leading the talks; Turkiye, which is hosting the meeting; and nearly 200 delegations from many of the world’s richest, poorest, largest and smallest nations.

Delegations had until 03:00 GMT on Sunday to ‌raise any objections to the deal, with a session scheduled at 06:00 GMT to ⁠begin approving ⁠it.

The summit’s agreement is meant to address how the world will deal with climate change, which drives heatwaves, floods and other disasters.

An opening draft from Australia on Monday called for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels. A slimmer version on Thursday removed every mention of them after Saudi Arabia and other major oil and gas producers objected.

Key issues that slowed down the agreement included how much effort countries should make to wean themselves off fossil fuels, such as coal, oil and gas.

Other issues included whether to encourage industrial carbon capture and storage of pollutants, as well as whether ramping up electricity should only be done with renewables, such as wind and solar, or also involve other sources like natural gas and coal.

To avert the most catastrophic effects of warming, experts said the world needs to urgently and drastically cut fossil fuel emissions.

The two-week talks in the Turkish city of Antalya were due to end on Friday.

In a letter sent on Saturday to this year’s cohosts, Turkiye and Australia, 100 civil society groups warned that they were “on course to preside over one of the most disappointing COPs” the UN has ever held.

The letter stated there were only hours left “to save this COP from becoming a low point of three decades of climate negotiations”.

In the lead-up to these talks, the United Nations said the world would likely blow past the 2015 Paris Agreement goal of limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial temperatures.
sources.headline: Fossil fuel impasse pushes COP31 climate talks into second day of overtime

sources.body:
Talks were set to resume at the UN COP31 summit on Sunday for a second day of overtime as countries struggle to reach a new global climate deal.

Nations were deadlocked in Turkey on how to advance the fight against global warming, after new draft agreements included no reference to reducing the world's demand for fossil fuels.

A third and "final" text was sent to delegates in the early hours of Sunday morning and members had until 06:00 local time (0300 GMT) to raise concerns before a 9am local time (0600GMT) meeting for approval.

If countries cannot reach consensus - as required by the UN's climate talks process - the negotiations could be suspended to reconvene next year.

A draft deal unveiled earlier this week called for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels, but a second, pared-down version released Thursday stripped away all mentions of coal, oil and gas - sparking threats of a walk out.

The fallout led to the summit in Antalya blowing past the original deadline of Friday . On Saturday negotiating teams who had Sunday morning flights were rescheduling them - a sign a deal was still not in sight, and raising the risk that as teams eventually had to leave, the meeting could lose the critical numbers needed to pass an agreement.

As part of a last ditch effort to produce an acceptable text, the European Union and Saudi Arabia - who were deeply divided over the future of fossil fuels - were brought together on Saturday to seek a compromise.

COP31 President and Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum told delegates in the early hours of Sunday morning he believed concerns had been addressed.

"We ask you to look at this decision carefully," Kurum said.

"We are closer than ever to agreement on the remaining issues."

If the countries can't agree, the summit would end with no deal and be reconvened next year.

This has only happened once before since countries started holding COP climate meetings in 1995.

Ministers from Panama, Solomon Islands, Cote d'Ivoire and the EU were fighting to have a commitment to move away from fossil fuels put back into the final agreement, after fossil fuel producers led by Saudi Arabia pushed for its removal.

"It is not acceptable to have a COP or a cover decision that does not even mention fossil fuels and we simply will not put up with it," said Juan Carlos Navarro, Panama's minister for the environment.

Tuvalu's Climate Minister Maina Talia told reporters it was a "red line" for the low-lying Pacific nation: "We're talking about the root cause of all of this".

France's Minister of Ecological Transition, Monique Barbut, took aim at several references in the text to carbon capture - a technology that takes emissions when they are released and stores them underground.

She said it was being used as a licence for other countries to keep burning oil and gas.

"We cannot be announcing to the world that we are now getting to 1.5 increase in the temperature and do business like nothing was happening," Barbut said.

For the first time at a COP, the agreement - known officially as the Antalya Accords - could acknowledge that the goal set under the Paris climate accord of keeping global temperature rise below 1.5C has been missed.
sources.headline: Fossil fuel dispute threatens to derail COP31 climate deal

sources.body: COP31 climate talks in Turkey have gone into overtime, with deep divisions over fossil fuels, climate finance and global warming targets delaying an agreement. A revised draft dropped all mention of fossil fuels, prompting strong criticism from the EU and a dozen countries demanding a clear commitment to phase them out. Negotiators are also split over a proposed global electrification target, carbon capture and the future of UN climate science reports. Developing nations have voiced anger over the removal of a $120 billion climate adaptation funding target. Australia is now racing to secure a revised deal before delegates leave. France 24 journalist Adria Rocha Cutiller tells us the latest.
sources.headline: COP31: Deep divisions persist over energy, finance and science

stories.headline: Bahrain reports Iranian attack and fire at an industrial facility

sources.body:
Bahrain reports no injuries, as Iran’s IRGC says it targeted US military positions at two bases in al-Riffa and Awali.

Bahrain has said an Iranian attack struck a civilian industrial facility, starting a fire, in the latest escalation of the war in the Middle East.

Bahrain’s air defences intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks late on Saturday, according to the Bahraini Defence Force.

In a post on X, Bahrain’s Ministry of Interior said the attack was part of “Iranian aggression”.

It said preliminary reports pointed to material damage but no injuries, and that civil defence teams were working to bring the fire under control.

The Interior Ministry did not name the facility or say where it was. Earlier, air raid sirens sounded in Bahrain, and the ministry urged residents to move to the nearest safe place without saying what the threat was.

In a statement after the attack, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it had carried out a combined missile and drone operation targeting United States military positions at the al-Riffa and Awali bases in Bahrain.

The IRGC claimed it destroyed two US Patriot air defence radars at the bases.

The attack was “in response to continued aggression and violations of the airspace of the Islamic Republic of Iran”, the statement said.

“After two US MQ-1 and MQ-9 reconnaissance and combat drones violated Iranian airspace, US military positions at the aforementioned bases were targeted in an operation by the IRGC Aerospace Force,” it added.

Earlier, Iran’s semi-official Fars news agency reported that the IRGC had attacked two military bases used by US forces at Sheikh Isa and Juffair.

The IRGC said that operation, as well as being in response to continued violations of Iranian airspace, came following a US attack on a radar installation on Iran’s Hengam Island.

Iran’s state news agency IRNA reported that an interceptor missile launched from the US Fifth Fleet base in Bahrain had also crashed on Sitra Island and started a large fire. It cited an outlet called Bahrain News, which blamed a recurring malfunction in the Patriot air defence system.

Bahrain hosts the US Navy’s Fifth Fleet. It has been attacked repeatedly since the US-Israel war on Iran began in late February, including three drone attacks in recent days after a lull of several weeks.

Bahrain issued an all-clear notice following the attack on the facility but urged residents to remain cautious.

Other Gulf states have also come under repeated fire from Tehran since the US-Israel war began.

In a statement on X, Bahrain’s Foreign Ministry called on the United Nations Security Council to take “firm measures to compel Iran” to implement Resolution 2817.

The resolution, adopted on March 11, condemns Iranian attacks against Gulf states and Jordan, and demands an immediate halt to hostilities and maritime interference.

The head of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) expressed his “full solidarity” with Bahrain following Iran’s attack on the industrial facility.

Jassim Mohamed AlBudaiwi, GCC secretary-general, said Bahrain’s security, territorial integrity, facilities, citizens and residents are an integral part of the security of the GCC states, and that the council stands united in confronting threats to their security and stability.
sources.headline: Bahrain says Iranian attack causes fire at industrial facility

stories.headline: International talks on regulating autonomous weapons collapse without a binding agreement

sources.body:
Week-long efforts fail to establish negotiating mandate on AI warfare after Russian ‘filibustering’

Week-long efforts to agree a negotiating mandate for a legally binding international treaty to control the use of autonomous weapons collapsed just before 5am after all-night talks failed to overcome Russian objections.

Despite an overwhelming majority of states at the UN’s Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) in Geneva wanting to agree a negotiating mandate leading to a legally binding treaty, the need for consensus forced the conference to adopt a much weaker option.

The mandate asked countries “to elaborate by consensus”, an instrument that may not carry any legal obligations.

Although Russia led the objections using obstructive stalling tactics, other military powers invested in AI warfare, such as the US, were reluctant to commit to a legally binding protocol protecting civilians from robot drones and other autonomous weapons.

Some argued that international humanitarian law was sufficient. More than 100 states had been pushing for a new law, saying the weapons raised entirely new challenges. European and Nato states, including Ukraine, China and Iran, expressed support or willingness for a new protocol.

The US said the need for human control over autonomous weapons had been discussed at the Apec summit in meetings between president Xi Jinping and Donald Trump this week, but the US was reluctant to agree a binding treaty.

South Korea, Japan, Turkey, the UK, France and Germany were among the defence tech powers exploring AI-enabled weapons who also expressed resistance to being bound by a new law, instead advocating for a nonbinding agreement.

The CCW is a UN forum that operates via consensus, meaning all 128 parties to the convention have to agree unanimously to pass a statement. The high threshold has resulted in the CCW failing to pass any new laws regulating weapons in the past 30 years and states seeking pathways elsewhere to pass treaties, such as the 2008 ban on cluster munitions.

The Future of Life Institute’s chair, Max Tegmark, said world leaders had failed to meet the moment this week. “Slaughterbots are already here,” he said. “Yet states have agreed it is sufficient to just talk about this for the 14th year.”

Diplomats inside the negotiations said Russia had been deliberately filibustering and not working in good faith, as opposed to the US delegates, who had been seeking a path to reach a consensus statement.

The exclusion of several nonmember countries from negotiations also prompted a rare protest in the chamber on the final day of the conference, with the Egyptian delegation shouting at the conference chair.

A digest of the morning's main headlines from the Europe edition emailed direct to you every week day

Israel and the US have also used AI-enabled targeting systems to conduct tens of thousands of strikes in Gaza and Iran, which have resulted in mass casualties. The Pentagon struck more than 1,000 targets in Iran on the first day of the war, and according to investigative media reports, the US military is aiming to carry out 1,000 AI-assisted targeting decisions per hour.
sources.headline: International UN talks on controlling use of autonomous weapons collapse

sources.body:
Un pelotón de soldados prueba un dron terrestre ametrallador en el frente de Ucrania / UKRAINE'S 65TH MECHANIZED BRIGADE PRESS SERVICE

La falta de un acuerdo vinculante para regular el uso de los llamados "robots asesinos" en zonas de conflicto ha generado inquietud entre la comunidad internacional . Representantes de los países presentes en la Conferencia de Revisión sobre Ciertas Armas Convencionales , celebrada esta semana en la sede de las Naciones Unidas en Ginebra, han alertado sobre los riesgos de no poner coto al desarrollo y despliegue de las armas operadas con inteligencia artificial (IA). Unas críticas a las que se han sumado organizaciones humanitarias y defensores de los derechos humanos.

"La tecnología avanza más rápido que la diplomacia ", ha lamentado el delegado de Brasil, Frederico Meyer , cuyo país ha impulsado sin éxito —junto a Austria, Bélgica, Irlanda, México, Nueva Zelanda y Panamá— un conjunto de normas para impedir o limitar la capacidad de las máquinas para matar sin control humano ni rendición de cuentas.

Los 128 países miembros de la Convención debían acordar por unanimidad la nueva regulación, pero las reticencias de Estados Unidos e Israel y la negativa de Rusia han impedido lograr avances significativos. Tras unas largas conversaciones que se han extendido hasta las 5:00 horas de este sábado, las partes han cerrado un acuerdo de mínimos en el que se comprometen a seguir negociando para alcanzar un pacto significativo antes de 2028.

Además de la oposición de Estados Unidos, Israel y Rusia, otros países destacados en el desarrollo de esta tecnología, como el Reino Unido, Francia, Alemania, Corea del Sur o Japón , también han mostrado sus reservas ante la aprobación de una nueva regulación, apostando en cambio por un acuerdo no vinculante . El resultado ha sido una nueva decepción para los defensores de los derechos humanos, que lamentan la falta de acuerdos a pesar de que este asunto está siendo discutido desde hace más de una década.

"A medida que los sistemas de inteligencia artificial demuestran su potencial para actuar más allá del control de quienes los desarrollan, prueban o utilizan , no hay tiempo que perder a la hora de establecer normas internacionales claras para el desarrollo y el uso de armas autónomas", ha indicado este sábado el Comité Internacional de la Cruz Roja a través de un comunicado. En la misma línea se ha posicionado Anna Hehir , especialista en inteligencia artificial del Future Life Institute , quien ha alertado de que hay "mucho en juego" y de que no hay tiempo para permitirse "dos años más de discusiones".

A pesar de las críticas, el presidente de la Conferencia, el suizo Julien Thoeni , ha celebrado la disposición de los países miembros a seguir negociando para alcanzar un acuerdo en un plazo de dos años. "Ha sido un acuerdo de último minuto que demuestra que en tiempos difíciles Ginebra es un lugar donde el diálogo y el compromiso siguen siendo posibles", ha asegurado. Más prudente ha sido la alta representante de la ONU para Asuntos de Desarme, Izumi Nakamitsu , quien ha recordado las aspiraciones del secretario general del organismo, António Guterres , de lograr un acuerdo vinculante antes de que termine el año.
sources.headline: La falta de un acuerdo vinculante para regular los "robots asesinos" genera inquietud entre la comunidad internacional

stories.headline: Drone attack sets Russian cargo ship ablaze in the Gulf of Finland

sources.body: A Russian cargo ship caught fire after ​being hit by drones in the Baltic Sea on Saturday and drifted into Finnish waters. Reporting from Kyiv, FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg notes that the ship is affiliated with a major Russian military logistics company. While Ukrainian authorities typically neither confirm nor deny responsibility, analysts cite a clear motive for the targeting, Cragg explains.
sources.headline: Drone attack sets Russian cargo ship ablaze in Gulf of Finland

sources.body:
A Russian cargo vessel bound for the country's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad has been hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland, Russian and Finnish authorities say.

The ship - the Sparta II - caught on fire after the strike on Saturday morning, before drifting into Finnish waters. Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely behind the attack. Kyiv has yet to comment.

"War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity," Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said. "Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor."

Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said two drones had been used, based on preliminary information, and there was "no threat" to the territory's supplies.

The Sparta II was sanctioned by the US in 2022 and Ukraine earlier this year, and is run by a Russian company, according to the Ukrainian and US governments.

The company says on its website that it was established within the structure of Russia's defence ministry in 2011 and since 2015 has been operating within the military construction complex.

Finland's coast guard said it had been alerted to the attack at around 08:50 local time (06:50 GMT) on Saturday and that the cargo vessel had been located approximately 50km west of the island of Suursaari in the Gulf of Finland.

This prompted "temporary aviation and maritime restrictions" around the area, Finnish border officials said.

Shortly after the incident, Finland's defence ministry said a Russian helicopter was suspected of violating the country's airspace, potentially linked to "rescue or tracking operations".

A Russian rescue vessel approached the ship and was told by the crew that they did not need to be evacuated, Kaliningrad's governor wrote on Telegram, adding: "The crew is currently carrying out the necessary work and plans to continue on its way."

The Finnish Border Guard later said the crew had been evacuated to another Russian vessel that was now already en route to Russia. The Russian rescue vessel had remained at the location of the stricken ship.

It added that no environmental damage had been detected and that there was no danger to maritime traffic or people.

Kaliningrad is a Russian exclave that sits between Poland and Lithuania.

Defence Minister Antti Häkkänen said that the Finnish Border Guard were responsible for the investigation into the attack and were co-operating with other relevant authorities.

Nato has also been informed, the defence ministry said.

The Baltic Sea has become a flashpoint in the Russia-Ukraine war, triggered when Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Ukraine has recently ramped up its long-range attacks against Russia beyond the front lines.

Earlier this month, a Ukrainian drone strike hit a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland .
sources.headline: Russia-bound ship attacked in Gulf of Finland

sources.body:
El carguero ruso ‘Sparta II’ atacado por drones, envuelto en humo en aguas del golfo de Finlandia, en una imagen facilitada por la Guardia Fronteriza finlandesa el 21 de noviembre del 2026 

Un buque de carga ruso que se dirigía hacia el enclave ruso de Kaliningrado, en el mar Báltico, fue alcanzado este sábado por drones en aguas internacionales del golfo de Finlandia, según informaron autoridades rusas y finlandesas. El incidente llevó a Finlandia a reforzar la seguridad en la zona y a notificarlo a los aliados de la OTAN.

El carguero Sparta II resultó dañado y se incendió al oeste de la isla rusa de Gogland, que se halla en la parte oriental del golfo a unos 40 kilómetros de la costa finlandesa. Tras el impacto de dos drones, el buque derivó hacia aguas territoriales finlandesas, informaron las Fuerzas de Defensa de Finlandia. “La situación no supone ningún peligro para el resto del tráfico marítimo”, añadió la Guardia Fronteriza finlandesa. La tripulación fue evacuada.

“La guerra se está extendiendo a nuestras zonas vecinas. Las autoridades finlandesas están gestionando la situación en el golfo de Finlandia, donde un ataque con drones ha alcanzado a un buque mercante ruso. Ucrania tiene derecho a luchar contra el agresor”, escribió el primer ministro finlandés, ­Petteri Orpo, en la red social X.

Pese a la alusión de Orpo al derecho de Ucrania a combatir, por lo pronto las autoridades finlandesas no especificaron el origen de los dos drones. Ni el Ministerio de Defensa, ni las fuerzas armadas, ni la Guardia Fronteriza facilitaron este sábado elementos para determinar su procedencia. La Guardia Fronteriza finlandesa puntualizó que “el Sparta II tiene vínculos con las fuerzas armadas rusas”.

El gobernador de la región rusa de Leningrado, Alexandr Drozdenko, sí señaló implícitamente a Kyiv al informar en Telegram del ataque “a unas tres millas náuticas de la frontera marítima rusa”, e indicar que en la noche del viernes al sábado Ucrania había atacado la región con 80 drones.

Mientras, el gobernador de Kaliningrado , Alexéi Besprozvánnykh, se apresuró a asegurar que lo ocurrido no supone ninguna amenaza para el abastecimiento del enclave. Un helicóptero ruso violó el espacio aéreo finlandés, informó el Ministerio de Defensa de Finlandia, que relacionó la incursión “con las operaciones de rescate o seguimiento” del carguero dañado.

El ataque pone de relieve cómo se le está complicando a Rusia canalizar sus exportaciones de crudo y alimentos a través del mar Báltico. Estas rutas marítimas están ganando importancia para transporte de grano.

Mientras, el secretario general de la OTAN, el neerlandés Mark Rutte, visitó este sábado Varsovia tras la caída el viernes de dos misiles y un dron rusos en territorio polaco, que el primer ministro polaco, Donald Tusk, calificó de “provocación intencionada”, pues se están realizando en Polonia maniobras militares de países de la Coalición de Voluntarios que apoya a Kyiv.

“La OTAN defenderá cada pulgada del territorio polaco”, dijo Rutte a periodistas, informa la agencia de noticias polaca PAP. El neerlandés prometió que la comandancia de la OTAN en Europa analizará lo sucedido “con el fin de poder introducir los cambios necesarios si fuera preciso”.
sources.headline: Un ataque de drones contra un carguero ruso en el mar Báltico acerca el conflicto a Finlandia

stories.headline: EU and Indonesia sign trade agreement eliminating almost all tariffs

sources.body: The European Union and Indonesia have signed a major trade deal, ten years after talks began.The agreement removes almost all tariffs between the EU and Southeast Asia's biggest economy: 98.5 per cent of them. For Europe, it means access to a market of 280 million people and a steadier supply of nickel for batteries. For Indonesia, easier exports of palm oil, textiles and footwear, and it arrives just before its current EU trade preferences end on the 1st of January. To discuss the deal Airlangga Hartarto, Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs in Indonesia joined us on the programme.
sources.headline: EU-Indonesia agreement sees the light after ten years of negotiations

stories.headline: Mexico captures cartel leader El Chapo Isidro in firefight that kills 11

sources.body: Mexico's military forces captured ​one of the most wanted suspected drug lords, Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro," the military announced on Saturday, after a deadly firefight that killed seven suspected attackers and four soldiers. Flores, one of the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives, was flown to Mexico City after his capture.
sources.headline: Mexico captures drug cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’ after deadly firefight

sources.body:
Fausto Isidro Meza Flores was one of FBI’s most wanted fugitives and evaded capture for more than a decade

The Mexican military captured one of the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives during a special forces raid in the Mexican state of Sinaloa on Friday night.

Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro”, was arrested along with two other alleged leaders of his gang after a gun battle that triggered widespread panic in the city of Guasave.

The alleged leader of a major drug-trafficking cartel, the Meza Flores Transnational Criminal Organization (TCO), he had managed to evade arrest for more than a decade, even though there was a reward of up to $5m (£3.8m) on his head.

His FBI “most wanted” poster states his organisation “is allegedly responsible for the possession, distribution and importation of large quantities of heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl and marijuana into the United States, and has predominately controlled drug production, transportation and distribution in several locations throughout Mexico”.

Mexico’s defence ministry also alleged he is the leader of the Beltrán Leyva criminal organisation, which is allied to the Mayos, one of two rival factions in the powerful Sinaloa cartel.

Meza Flores’s alleged second-in-command, Germán N, whose alias is “Serafín”, and José N, an alleged financial operator for the Beltrán Leyva group, were also arrested.

The operation to capture the men was carried out by “elite military forces” with help from US intelligence, according to Mexico’s defence ministry.

After arriving in the “target area … using stealth and surprise”, the ministry said the arresting force came under attack “with gunfire and explosives” but managed to enter a house and make the arrests.

The men were then evacuated to Mexico City on a Mexican air force plane to be handed over to prosecutors.

Videos and photos show civilians fleeing gunfire at a baseball game at Kuroda Park stadium in Guasave, as well as burnt-out cars.

A barrage of rapid fire from what appeared to be Mexican security force helicopters hit the ground, according to CNN, and players from the Venados de Mazatlán and Algodoneros de Guasave teams abandoned the field mid-game.

Four Mexican army infantry soldiers died in the operation, the defence ministry said in a statement posted on X that extended the institution’s condolences to their families.

It added that security forces killed seven attackers and arrested eight alleged criminals in the operation, including three who were transferred to Mexico City and five who were turned over to the attorney general’s office in Culiacán, Sinaloa.

Overnight on Friday the ​military operation triggered a wave of violence in the state of Sinaloa, including armed ‌clashes between Mexican security forces and cartel members, who ‌set up flaming roadblocks in some areas.

By ​Saturday the violence had substantially subsided. Sinaloa state authorities ​said “the situation is under control and being addressed by all levels of government”.

Meza Flores was originally indicted in 2012, and in 2013 the US Treasury placed sanctions on him under the Kingpin Act, freezing his assets.
sources.headline: Alleged Mexican drug cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’ arrested in special forces raid

sources.body:
Seven alleged cartel gunmen and four soldiers were killed in the operation to arrest Fausto Isidro Meza Flores.

The operation to capture Mexican cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores in the country’s Sinaloa state has left at least 11 people dead.

Mexico’s Defence Ministry said on Saturday that seven alleged cartel gunmen and four Mexican soldiers were killed in the overnight operation.

Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro”, was captured on Friday and flown to Mexico City on Saturday after hours-long violence involving a firefight between Mexican forces and cartel gunmen overnight, roadblocks and burning trucks in the city of Guasave.

Two other men were also captured and flown to Mexico City. The ministry identified them as German N, known as “Serafin”, the group’s alleged second-in-command, and Jose N, an alleged financial operator of the cartel. Both were also flown to Mexico City and handed over to prosecutors.

Meza Flores, one of the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives, climbed the ranks to lead the Beltrán Leyva cartel and later became the boss of his own group, the Meza-Flores transnational criminal organisation.

He was also a key ally to “Los Mayos”, a faction of the Sinaloa Cartel, which the United States designated as a “foreign terrorist organization” last year.

The US wanted Meza Flores for trafficking drugs to the country and offered a $5m reward for information leading to his arrest.

The firefight in Guasave broke out about 7pm on Friday (02:00 GMT on Saturday), according to residents. Military helicopters and drones were soon flying overhead, with helicopters opening fire on key locations across the city.

Videos show screaming civilians fleeing gunfire at a baseball game, burning cars and businesses, and circling helicopters shooting at people below.

Because of the violence, the Mexican army and National Guard special forces were unable to extract Meza Flores from Guasave until 4am (11:00 GMT) on Saturday, said a federal official who spoke on condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to discuss the case.

While a tense calm has settled over Guasave since the operation, experts warned that picking off cartel bosses could set off more waves of violence in a region already caught up in a power struggle between warring factions.

Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has been under pressure from US President Donald Trump to crack down on cartels and has gone after illegal groups more aggressively than her predecessors. Homicides have dipped significantly in her two years in office.

The US Drug Enforcement Administration commended Mexican authorities, as did Washington’s ambassador to Mexico.

“Results like these don’t happen overnight. They are built on sustained cooperation and trust. This is what partners can accomplish together,” US Ambassador Ronald Johnson said in an X post.
sources.headline: Eleven killed in burst of violence during Mexican cartel leader’s capture

stories.headline: FBI investigates suspected breach of its national crime database

sources.body:
The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its criminal information database, US media reports, citing two people briefed on the issue.

The National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information on warrants and background checks.

It would not be the first time hackers have targeted the FBI, the domestic intelligence and security service of the US. The agency did not respond to the BBC's request for comment.

When asked about the breach in a Fox News interview on Saturday, President Donald Trump said he had "just heard" about the hack. "I will say that it's not good. I don't like that," he said.

"But maybe we'll learn things that we would've never learned otherwise," Trump added.

This apparent breach of FBI database comes after a string of tech outages which hit banking, air traffic control and other sectors in the US last week. Officials have said they were not caused by cyber-attacks, but the blackouts have sparked scrutiny from lawmakers.

White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was fired this week, with Trump saying he was not good enough.

Dan Lorhmann, a former analyst for the National Security Agency (NSA), told the BBC News Channel that the NCIC's data included "critical information relating to nationwide criminal activity" and needed to be protected.

He added that while US security agencies including the FBI have "an amazing ability" to keep such information safe" and are "globally respected", the level of cyber-attacks is rising globally.

"There's a lot of different reasons why that's happening but I do have faith in our experts in government," Lorhmann said.

In September, the FBI said it was investigating an apparent breach by a cyber-crime group ShinyHunters, which claimed it had stolen sensitive information on all bureau staff - around 38,000 people.

After that hack, one former FBI agent told the BBC he feared for the safety of current employees, whose personal information could soon become available online to criminals and hostile nation-state hackers.

In a separate development, NBC reported an apparent cyberattack against the US Department of Agriculture (USDA).

Employees were informed on Thursday that its farm payment system had been targeted, NBC said.

The USDA has not publicly commented on the issue.
sources.headline: FBI reportedly investigating apparent hack of its criminal database

sources.body:
The reported hacking is the latest in ​a string of breaches and outages affecting the US government.

The FBI’s national criminal database has suffered a suspected breach, according to multiple US media reports.

President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly downplayed breaches affecting departments within his administration, appeared to confirm the FBI hacking during a television interview on Saturday.

“Well, we just heard about it, and I will say that it’s not good. I don’t like that,” Trump told Fox News.

On Friday, CNN and NBC reported that the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which is used by law enforcement agencies across the United States to share information on criminal warrants and background checks, was compromised, citing two people who had been briefed on the matter.

The reported hacking, which would be the second to hit the bureau this year, is the latest in a string of US government breaches and outages that have alarmed officials over the past week.

In a separate incident, NBC reported an apparent cyberattack against the US Department of Agriculture.

The FBI and USDA did not immediately return Al Jazeera’s request for comment.

In the interview on Saturday, Trump suggested the hack of the FBI’s crucial database could be viewed with “a positive spin”.

“Maybe we’ll learn things that we would have never learned otherwise. You had the Russia, Russia, Russia hoax. You had all these other hoaxes,” he said in an apparent reference to his discontent with the FBI’s investigation into Russian interference in the 2016 US election.

In September, the FBI said it was investigating an apparent breach by a cyber group that claimed it had stolen sensitive information on the bureau’s 38,000 employees.

Additionally, in March, the agency said it had been investigating “suspicious activities” on some of its internal systems, The Associated Press news agency reported.

FBI Director Kash Patel, who has not publicly commented on the most recent hacking, was not present for a Wednesday hearing at the US Capitol to examine threats against the US. Patel’s deputy, Christopher Raia, attended in his place, joining US Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton.
sources.headline: FBI national crime database suffers suspected breach: Reports

sources.body: The FBI is investigating a reported major cyberattack targeting its national law enforcement database, the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which holds sensitive criminal justice records, including information on fugitives, missing persons, criminal histories and stolen property. President Donald Trump said he had just been briefed on the incident, describing it as “not good”. FRANCE 24’s Fraser Jackson reports from Washington DC.
sources.headline: FBI criminal database hacked

stories.headline: New polls give Spain’s right-wing bloc a majority a week before the election

sources.body:
La pugna por la primera plaza sigue abierta; en cambio, la mayoría de PP y Vox parece muy decantada

Las elecciones las pierden los gobiernos y no parece que el 29-N vaya a ser una excepción, a la vista del sondeo de Ipsos para  La Vanguardia  , realizado entre los días 13 y 20 de noviembre sobre una muestra de 1.999 entrevistas. Sin embargo, con una participación estimada de hasta el 74%, la en apariencia inexorable mayoría conservadora (de en torno a 190 escaños) no deja de sorprender en un país en el que el bloque de la derecha nunca ha ganado en voto absoluto unos comicios con niveles de afluencia a las urnas por encima del 70%.

En cualquier caso, los distintos indicadores reflejan con precisión el nivel de desgaste del Gobierno de coalición progresista, aunque la correlación final se vea muy condicionada por el espectacular ascenso de la ultraderecha (de más de siete puntos entre Vox y SALF) y el notable retroceso del conjunto de la izquierda radical, lastrada por su aguda fragmentación. Paralelamente, los dos grandes partidos libran una feroz pugna por la primera plaza, ya que ambos retroceden con respecto a los resultados del 2023, aunque lo hace en mayor medida (tres puntos) el Partido Popular. Esta evolución deja al PSOE (con el 29,8%) a apenas medio punto del PP (30,3%), lo que se traduciría en 127 escaños para los populares (11 menos que hace tres años), frente a 119 para el PSOE (dos menos). De hecho, las respectivas horquillas podrían situar a los socialistas por delante (con hasta 124 diputados frente a un mínimo de 118 para el PP).

El reflujo del partido de Feijóo no explica, sin embargo, el avance de la ultraderecha, que se alimenta también de votantes procedentes de la abstención y de uno cada cinco nuevos electores. En el otro extremo, la dispersión de la izquierda alternativa agudiza el impacto de su retroceso (de entre cinco y tres puntos si también se contempla la eclosión de Adelante Andalucía) y penaliza la traducción de sus votos en escaños. De los 31 diputados que logró Sumar en el 2023, ahora reuniría diez en el mejor de los casos (y un total de 15 si se incluye el resultado de los andalucistas de izquierdas).

En realidad, el descalabro de la izquierda alternativa (que se materializa en la probable desaparición parlamentaria de Podemos) contribuye a maquillar las pérdidas del PSOE. El partido de Sánchez registra una fidelidad de voto del 64% (cinco puntos menos que el PP y 15 menos que Vox) y sufre pérdidas hacia la derecha (de hasta un 8% de sus votantes del 2023) y de similar magnitud hacia su izquierda (con especial intensidad en Andalucía).

Ahora bien, la debacle de la izquierda radical se refleja en unas cifras muy concretas: solo un 41% de quienes votaron a Sumar lo hará el 29-N por el Frente Amplio y únicamente un 4% apoyará a Podemos. En cambio, el 7% lo hará por Adelante Andalucía y, atención, uno de cada cuatro (el 27%) se inclinará ahora por el PSOE. Aun así, y frente a los 190 escaños de promedio de la derecha, el conjunto del espacio progresista reuniría 132 diputados, 20 menos que en el 2023 (con un máximo de 138 frente al mínimo de 184 del bloque conservador).
sources.headline: La derecha suma mayoría absoluta mientras el PSOE se acerca al PP

stories.headline: Sánchez announces plan to extend bank tax through 2027 to fund public housing

sources.body:
Pedro Sánchez, durante su entrevista en Onda Cero

Pedro Sánchez no quiere desaprovechar ni un día, ya en la recta final de la campaña electoral. El presidente del Gobierno ha anunciado este sábado que el Consejo de Ministros del próximo martes, el último antes de la cita con las urnas del próximo 29 de noviembre, viene con “sorpresa”.

“Vamos a prorrogar el impuesto a la banca al año 2027”, ha confirmado Sánchez en el programa de Julia Otero en Onda Cero. Este gravamen a los beneficios extraordinarios de los bancos expiraba a finales de este 2026, pero el Gobierno lo ampliará también para el año que viene.

“Eso va a significar que vamos a recaudar 1.400 millones de euros, que vamos a destinar íntegramente a la construcción de vivienda protegida, a bonificaciones fiscales a los inquilinos y también a la rehabilitación de viviendas”, ha asegurado el jefe del Ejecutivo.

Toda la recaudación de este impuesto extraordinario se dedicará, por tanto, a la política de vivienda, según ha garantizado Sánchez, ya que se trata de una de las principales preocupaciones de la ciudadanía. Fuentes del Gobierno han explicado que con la prórroga del gravamen a la banca se prevé una recaudación de 1.400 millones de euros, y “se establecerá por ley que se destinen a políticas de vivienda”.

Según las cifras que baraja el Ejecutivo, con esta recaudación se podría financiar la construcción de más de 6.000 pisos asequibles, rehabilitar hasta 52.000 viviendas y aplicar bonificaciones fiscales a casi 120.000 inquilinos durante la próxima legislatura.

Sánchez ha advertido que el anuncio de la prórroga de este impuesto no debería ser mal recibido por el sector bancario. “No creo que la banca española tenga motivos para quejarse”, ha resaltado, ante unos beneficios que siguen creciendo año tras año. “Cuando uno mira las cuentas de resultados, ve que la banca ha ganado su dinero con este gobierno socialcomunista que dicen algunos de la derecha”, ha ironizado.

“En el juego, siempre gana la banca”, ha asegurado el líder del PSOE en el nuevo vídeo electoral que ha difundido hoy con motivo de este anuncio. “Pero la democracia no es un juego. En democracia, quien tiene que ganar es la gente”, ha advertido. “Por eso, en el próximo Consejo de Ministros vamos a prorrogar el impuesto a la banca, y el 100% de lo recaudado irá destinado a la promoción de vivienda protegida”, ha recalcado.

Madrid, 1966. Redactor de La Vanguardia en Madrid desde 1997
sources.headline: El Gobierno prorrogará un año el impuesto a la banca para políticas de vivienda

sources.body: El temps corre i dissabte de la setmana que ve la campanya electoral del 29-N ja haurà acabat. Per això, aquest cap de setmana els partits premen l’accelerador i alguns, com Front Ampli, han celebrat el seu acte gros. Destaquen la presència d’Ada Colau a Barcelona per primer cop en nou dies de campanya, anuncis de Sánchez per allargar mesures que ha pres el seu govern en cas de no revalidar el càrrec i retrets encreuats dels partits independentistes. Et desgranem els titulars principals de la jornada. Per saber-ne més Tota la informació de les eleccions generals del 29-N Consulta totes les dades i notícies disponibles Sánchez (PSOE) anuncia la pròrroga de l’impost a la banca El president del Govern espanyol i candidat a la reelecció, Pedro Sánchez , ha començat el dia anunciant que el Consell de Ministres de dimarts, 24 de novembre, aprovarà la pròrroga de l’impost a la banca fins al 2027. Ho ha dit en una entrevista a Onda Cero. Amb el que es recapti (1.400 milions d’euros, segons l’executiu espanyol) es construirà habitatge protegit . També aquest dissabte al matí, Sánchez ha participat en un acte a Santa Cruz de Tenerife, des d’on ha fet una crida a la mobilització per arribar al 75 % de la participació , el necessari, ha dit, per arribar a “ 176 escons progressistes “. El cap de llista del PSC per Barcelona, Jordi Hereu , i el president de la Generalitat i primer secretari del PSC, Salvador Illa , han participat en un acte a Lleida. Els socialistes centren esforços en aquesta província per guanyar-hi dos diputats “estratègics” que, segons Hereu, “obriran l’Espanya progressista”. Pedro Sánchez a Santa Cruz de Tenerife. Foto: PSOE Primer acte de Colau (Front Ampli) a Barcelona Front Ampli ha fet aquest dissabte el seu acte central, que ha estat doblement rellevant perquè ha suposat el retorn a Barcelona de l’exalcaldessa Ada Colau , que fins ara no havia fet campanya a la ciutat. Els frontamplistes han omplert el Parc de Sant Martí , un districte que ha donat bons resultats a l’entorn dels comuns les últimes eleccions generals i municipals. Han acompanyat Colau altres noms forts de la formació, com el número dos a la llista de Barcelona (Ernest Urtasun), el candidat per Madrid (Emilio Delgado), l’alcaldable de BComú a Barcelona (Gerardo Pisarello) i la ministra de Treball (Yolanda Díaz). Des de Sant Martí, Colau ha avisat al PSC/PSOE: “Ens presentem per fer allò que el Partit Socialista diu que no es pot fer, com regular l’habitatge… Ho vam fer a Barcelona i ho farem a l’Estat “. Gerardo Pisarello, Ernest Urtasun, Yolanda Díaz, Ada Colau i Emilio Delgado, a Barcelona. Foto: ACN Feijóo (PP), des d’una plaça de toros: “Tinc la fam d’un noveller” El popular Alberto Núñez Feijóo ha omplert la plaça de bous de València i, com si fos un torero, ha assegurat: “Tinc la fam d’un noveller després de 30 anys a l’arena i després de més d’una cornada”. Alhora, ha fet una crida a la mobilització als seus simpatitzants i els ha demanat que no es refiïn de les enquestes . “Els coneixem: són capaços de tot i ferits són encara més perillosos “, ha etzibat encara amb el símil del món taurí. Al mateix acte també hi ha participat el president de la Generalitat Valenciana, Juanfran Pérez Llorca, i ha criticat Compromís i ERC per “somiar amb els Països Catalans “. Llorca ha dit: “Nosaltres som valencians i espanyols”. Alberto Núñez Feijóo, a València. Foto: ACN A Alamany (ERC) li fa “molta vergonya” Junts A la plaça de la Virreina de Gràcia, la secretària general d’ERC, Elisenda Alamany , ha reivindicat el vot a ERC com a garantia per evitar un govern del PP i Vox. I la republicana ha carregat contra el seu rival independentista: Junts . Alamany ha dit que li fa “molta vergonya” quan els de Miriam Nogueras diuen que se situen “al mig”, especialment per les “ amenaces cap al poble català i cap als drets de les dones ” que suposen PP i Vox. “El que necessitem ara és un mur per defensar Catalunya”, ha dit. La vicepresidenta del partit, Diana Riba , la vicesecretària general de Feminismes i LGTBI+ d’ERC (i també regidora del partit a l’Ajuntament), Eva Baró , i altres dones de les llistes de la formació a les generals del 29-N han acompanyat a Alamany en l’acte, que ha estat en defensa dels drets de les dones . Elisenda Alamany i dones membres d’ERC, a la plaça de la Virreina de Gràcia. Foto: ACN Nogueras (Junts): “Tornarem els diners dels catalans a Catalunya” Des de Vic, la candidata de Junts a la presidència, Miriam Nogueras , ha reiterat que Junts treballarà per atorgar més competències a Catalunya i, en aquest sentit, ha carregat contra ERC per aliar-se amb Podem, “un partit espanyol que ha votat amb PP-Vox en contra de que els catalans tinguem les competències en immigració “, ha dit. Nogueras també ha promès una nova llei del padró per evitar l’empadronament de persones sense una situació administrativa regularitzada. I també ha assegurat: “Aquesta legislatura la gent de Junts tornarem els diners dels catalans a Catalunya. Els impostos que paguem els catalans els hem de gestionar, recaptar i decidir des de Catalunya”. Miriam Nogueras, a Vic. Foto: ACN Mejías (Vox): “La prioritat nacional és fer fora a Sánchez” Aquest dissabte Vox ha celebrat un acte a la plaça de Molina (a Sant Gervasi – Galvany) i ha comptat amb la participació del president del Grup Municipal de Vox a l’Ajuntament de Barcelona, Gonzalo de Oro. Ha denunciat “el deteriorament” de la seguretat a Barcelona i ha acusat l’alcalde, Jaume Collboni, d’oferir un relat allunyat de la realitat dels veïns. De Oro ha demanat mesures més contundents contra els multireincidents i l’ ocupació il·legal , així com una reducció de la pressió fiscal . D’altra banda, la número dos de Vox per Barcelona al Congrés dels Diputats, Carina Mejías , ha assegurat: “L’únic vot útil que hi ha és el vot a Vox, perquè sense Vox no hi haurà canvi”. En aquest sentit, ha dit: “La prioritat nacional és fer fora a Sánchez i el seu govern corrupte , mentider i traïdor “. Carina Mejías i Gonzalo de Oro, a Barcelona. stories.headline: Hydrogen supply failure sidelines 23 Barcelona buses, reducing service on X1, V19 and D20

sources.body: (ACN/Redacció) Un problema tècnic a la planta d’hidrogen d’Iberdrola de la Zona Franca ha deixat 23 autobusos de TMB fora de servei . Ho han avançat els diaris Ara i La Vanguardia i ho han confirmat fonts de TMB a l’ACN. La companyia ha apuntat que l’avaria té un impacte limitat en el servei , atès que només 46 dels 896 vehicles de la flota funcionen amb aquest combustible, un 5 % del total. Així, la reducció de l’oferta se situa entre el 2,5 % i el 3,8 %, fet que implica que, en algunes línies, els usuaris han d’esperar nou minuts en lloc de set que arribi l’autobús . TMB també ha assegurat que la companyia energètica li ha confirmat que la incidència quedarà resolta d’aquí a poques setmanes. També et pot interessar Què passa quan el bus acaba el servei? La feina invisible de les cotxeres de TMB Bernat Martínez Lacorte 2 minuts de lectura L’X1, V19 i D20, les línies més afectades La incidència és, sobretot, en algunes línies que utilitzaven aquest model d’autobús, principalment l’ X1, la V19 i la D20 , i n’ha alterat les freqüències de pas. En la majoria dels casos, els usuaris han passat d’esperar set minuts a esperar-ne nou entre vehicles. L’estació de servei d’hidrogen de la Zona Franca es va posar en funcionament fa gairebé cinc anys, a principis del 2022. Des de l’inici, TMB va arribar a un acord per rebre subministrament d’hidrogen per als seus autobusos, quan en tenia només vuit, a canvi de 14,5 milions d’euros en 10 anys. També et pot interessar L’X1 amplia el recorregut i ja connecta les Glòries amb la Zona Universitària Maria Solans 1 minut de lectura Els sindicats diuen que la incidència és molt superior Fonts sindicals han assegurat que l’afectació en el servei de bus és superior a la comunicada per TMB i que la situació es podria allargar fins al febrer. A més, han criticat que les obres de la Línia 2 del metro també tenen incidència en el servei d’autobusos, ja que TMB hi està destinant vehicles per reforçar el transport alternatiu. Els sindicats han lamentat que la coincidència de les dues situacions provoqui “una retallada molt important” del servei .
sources.headline: 23 autobusos de TMB fora de servei per l’aturada de la planta d’hidrogen de la Zona Franca

sources.body:
Archivo - Logotipo de TMB / Lorena Sopêna - Europa Press - Archivo

Un problema técnico en la planta de hidrógeno de Iberdrola de la Zona Franca ha dejado 23 autobuses de TMB fuera de servicio, según ha avanzado 'ARA' y 'La Vanguardia' y ha confirmado ACN. La compañía ha señalado que la avería tiene un impacto "limitado" en el servicio, dado que solo 46 de los 896 vehículos de la flota funcionan con este combustible, lo que representa un 5 % del total. Así, la reducción de la oferta se sitúa entre el 2,5 % y el 3,8 %, lo que implica que, en algunas líneas, los usuarios tienen que esperar nueve minutos en lugar de siete.

TMB también ha asegurado que la compañía energética le ha confirmado que la incidencia quedará resuelta "en pocas semanas". La incidencia ha afectado principalmente a algunas líneas que utilizaban este modelo de autobús, especialmente la X1, la V19 y la D20, y ha alterado sus frecuencias de paso. En la mayoría de los casos, los usuarios han pasado de esperar siete minutos a esperar nueve entre autobuses.

La estación de servicio de hidrógeno de la Zona Franca entró en funcionamiento hace casi cinco años, a principios de 2022. Desde el inicio, TMB llegó a un acuerdo para recibir suministro de hidrógeno para sus autobuses, cuando solo disponía de ocho vehículos de este tipo, a cambio de 14,5 millones de euros en diez años.

Fuentes sindicales han asegurado que el impacto en el servicio de autobuses urbanos de Barcelona por la falta de suministro de hidrógeno es superior al comunicado por TMB y que la situación podría prolongarse hasta febrero.

Además, han criticado que las obras de la línea 2 del metro también estén afectando al servicio de autobuses , ya que TMB está destinando vehículos a reforzar el transporte alternativo. El tramo entre las estaciones de La Pau y Gorg permanece c ortado desde el 2 de noviembre y hasta el 3 de diciembre para reparar una incidencia que afecta a la plataforma de la vía.

Los sindicatos han lamentado que la coincidencia de ambas situaciones esté provocando "un recorte muy importante" del servicio.
sources.headline: Una avería en la planta de hidrógeno de la Zona Franca deja 23 autobuses de TMB fuera de servicio
